question: Does delta key-index maintenance improve end-to-end keyed structural updates when keyed child components own local state, compared with the prior subtree-rescan algorithm in the same compiled component-state runtime?

hypotheses.primary: Delta key-index maintenance will reduce within-page median update time relative to subtree rescanning for rotate, edge replacement, and each direction of half filtering.
hypotheses.contextual: React + Compiler provides a same-page contextual comparison; it is not the causal contrast because the runtime algorithms differ only within the runtime arms.

design.armOrder: All six arm permutations are balanced over 32 update pairs per operation, then seed-shuffled; raw pair order is archived.
design.measurement: Click through commit completion: React flushSync; runtime arms include the scheduled microtask commit. Mount and teardown are timed separately once per arm and operation.
design.replicationUnit: Fresh visible browser page; update samples within a page are repeated measures, not independent replications.
design.browserProfile: One Chrome MacIntel profile and one device; environment recorded by each page.

primaryEndpoints: Within-page median paired difference and ratio for rebuild versus delta, by operation; filter samples additionally stratified by explicit direction.
Number of pages where delta has a lower within-page median for each operation and filter direction.
secondaryEndpoints: React context median and p95 update times.
Per-arm update p95, mount, and teardown time.
Combined mount + 24 updates + teardown per arm, reported descriptively with no exclusions.
contracts: All three arms produce identical ordered rows and selected-state output after every pair.
Retained keys preserve host identity; removed keys detach; reinserted keys receive fresh host identity and initial local state.
Every page is visible, uses 10,000 rows, and records 8 warmups plus 24 measured pairs for each operation.
All six arm orders appear four or five times in each 32-pair operation schedule; no performance-based exclusion.
limitations: One browser/device profile and five page replications do not establish hardware or browser generality.
The measurement ends at synchronous DOM commit and excludes layout, paint, and display presentation.
Mount and teardown have one timing observation per arm and operation; lifecycle totals are descriptive.
This isolates keyed index maintenance inside a stateful owner benchmark but does not represent a complete application.
